hypothesis: Two-slab K-loop unrolling with two tl.load A, two tl.load B, and two tl.dot per loop trip and 2*BK pointer advances will outperform baseline by halving loop iterations and amortizing loop overhead.
expected_mechanism: Each trip issues tl.load a0/b0 plus tl.dot a0,b0 then tl.load a1 from a_ptrs+BK and b1 from b_ptrs+BK*N plus tl.dot a1,b1 into FP32 acc, then single a_ptrs += BK*2 and b_ptrs += BK*2*N updates. This halves branch and mask-address recomputation versus one tl.dot per trip, keeps the same FP16 tl.load / FP32 tl.dot / FP16 tl.store semantics, and gives the num_stages=3 pipeliner two independent load-dot chains per trip to overlap.
reasoning_from_feedback: This differs from the prior unevaluated review which used a K-bound-specialized single tl.dot per full trip with hoisted m_mask/n_mask and separate tail tl.load/tl.dot, and differs from reviewed grouped_m4 and split_k structural kernels which changed only CTA ordering or K-parallelism. No compilation, correctness, or timing result exists for the prior candidate, so no measured feedback is claimed; this proposal instead changes inner K-loop organization and operand-loading/dot density while retaining baseline program-ID mapping and full per-slab M/N/K masks for boundary shapes.
